ground.reason: PRM-A1 checks the complete role/action matrix only on the populated fixture. It does not establish that authorization follows the same matrix for projects with no comments.

objections.objection: The criteria allow authorization to depend on whether the project has comments.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the viewer's edit succeeds and changes the empty project's body.
scenario.given: An implementation follows D1 on the prescribed fixture but allows every project member to edit projects with no comments.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and a viewer then edits an existing project with no comments.

ground.reason: PRM-A1 observes allowed reads of the populated fixture. An allowed read of a project with no comments can fail to return that project while every check passes.

objections.objection: The criteria allow an allowed read to omit project content outside the fixture.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the allowed read omits the project's body.
scenario.given: An implementation returns the complete project for the prescribed fixture but omits the body whenever its comments list is empty.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and an owner then reads an existing project with no comments.

ground.reason: PRM-A1 checks appending a comment after two existing comments. It does not check adding the first comment.

objections.objection: The criteria allow an allowed comment request to succeed without adding the first comment.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the request returns 2xx and the project's comments remain empty.
scenario.given: An implementation appends comments when comments already exist but discards comments submitted to an empty comments list.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and a commenter then submits the first comment to an existing project.

ground.reason: PRM-A1 observes body replacement only on the populated fixture. Projects with no comments are outside that check's represented cases.

objections.objection: The criteria allow an allowed edit to leave the previous body in place.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the edit returns 2xx and the owner subsequently reads the old body.
scenario.given: An implementation replaces the body on the prescribed fixture but ignores edits when the project's comments list is empty.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and an owner then edits an existing project with no comments.

ground.reason: PRM-A1 checks removal of the populated fixture. It does not establish removal of projects with no comments.

objections.objection: The criteria allow an allowed delete to report success while retaining the project.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the delete returns 2xx and the owner's next read still returns the project.
scenario.given: An implementation removes the prescribed fixture but retains projects with no comments when processing an allowed delete.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and an owner then deletes an existing project with no comments.

ground.reason: PRM-A1 checks refusal responses for the five refused pairings on the populated fixture. The promised response also applies to those pairings on projects with no comments.

objections.objection: The criteria allow a refused action to return the wrong status and body.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the refused request returns HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 403 with the forbidden error body.
scenario.given: An implementation returns the specified refusal on the prescribed fixture but returns HTTP 500 for forbidden actions on projects with no comments.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and a viewer then attempts to delete an existing project with no comments.

ground.reason: PRM-A2 establishes preservation for the five refused pairings on the populated fixture. It leaves preservation on projects with no comments unchecked.

objections.objection: The criteria allow a refused action to change an empty comments list.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the refused request returns the specified 403 response and the owner's subsequent read contains an added comment.
scenario.given: An implementation preserves the prescribed fixture on refusal but inserts a blank comment when refusing an action on a project with no comments.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and a viewer then attempts to comment on an existing project with no comments.

ground.reason: PRM-A3 compares no-role responses with nonexistent-project responses only for the populated fixture and prescribed request history. It does not establish equivalence for projects with no comments.

objections.objection: The criteria allow a no-role response to reveal that an empty project exists.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the existing project's response is HTTP 403 while the same action on a nonexistent project returns HTTP 404.
scenario.given: An implementation matches nonexistent-project responses for the prescribed fixture but returns HTTP 403 to no-role callers for projects with no comments.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and a caller with no role then reads an existing project with no comments and a nonexistent project.

ground.reason: PRM-A3 establishes preservation after no-role requests only on the populated fixture. A no-role request can mutate a project with no comments without failing any criterion.

objections.objection: The criteria allow a no-role action to change the project while returning the required concealed response.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes and the no-role response matches the nonexistent-project response, but the owner subsequently reads a cleared body.
scenario.given: An implementation preserves the prescribed fixture but clears the body of projects with no comments when handling a no-role edit.
scenario.when: The integration checks run, and a caller with no role then attempts to edit an existing project with no comments.

obligations.statement: For callers holding viewer, commenter or owner roles, each action is allowed or refused according to the caller's role on the requested project and D1's matrix.
obligations.source: “The project API decides each of its four actions by the caller's role on the project, as the matrix in D1 gives.” D1: “A viewer may read. A commenter may read and comment. An owner may do all four. Every other pairing of role and action is refused.”

parts.statement: The twelve role/action pairings follow D1 in the freshly seeded P scenarios, including the prescribed preceding reads of Q.
The matrix also holds for existing projects and request histories outside those scenarios, including projects with no comments.

obligations.statement: An allowed read returns the project.
obligations.source: D1: “An allowed read returns the project”.

parts.statement: Allowed reads in PRM-A1's scenarios return P's seeded title, body, comments and revision list.
Allowed reads return the project outside those scenarios, including when its comments list is empty.

obligations.statement: An allowed comment adds the submitted comment to the project.
obligations.source: D1: “an allowed comment adds the comment to it”.

parts.statement: Allowed comments in PRM-A1's scenarios append the submitted comment after the two seeded comments, which remain.
Allowed comments are added outside those scenarios, including the first comment on a project.

obligations.statement: An allowed edit replaces the project's body with the submitted body.
obligations.source: D1: “an allowed edit replaces its body with the one sent”.

parts.statement: The allowed edit in PRM-A1's scenario changes the seeded project's body to the submitted body.
Allowed edits replace the body outside that scenario, including on projects with no comments.

obligations.statement: An allowed delete removes the project.

parts.statement: The allowed delete in PRM-A1's scenario removes the seeded project, as observed by every caller's next read returning 404.
Allowed deletes remove projects outside that scenario, including projects with no comments.

obligations.statement: Each refused pairing for a caller holding a project role returns HTTP 403 with the forbidden error body.
obligations.source: D2: “A refused action returns HTTP 403 with the body `{"error": "forbidden"}`”. D3 separately specifies the response for callers with no role.

parts.statement: The five refused pairings return the specified status and body in PRM-A1's seeded-project scenarios.
Those refused pairings return the specified status and body outside those scenarios, including on projects with no comments.

obligations.statement: A refused action preserves the project as subsequently read by an owner.
obligations.source: “A refused action leaves the project as it was.” D2: “the project, as an owner reads it afterwards, is unchanged.”

parts.statement: For each of the five refused pairings in PRM-A2's scenarios, the owner's subsequent view of the seeded project's title, body, comments and revision list is byte-identical.
Refused actions preserve the owner's view outside those scenarios, including when the project initially has no comments.

obligations.statement: For all four actions, a caller with no role receives the same response as for a nonexistent project, except that Date and X-Request-Id values may differ while their formats match.
obligations.source: D3: “A caller with no role on the project gets, for each of the four actions, the same response a request for a project that does not exist gets, apart from the values of the `Date` and `X-Request-Id` headers, which have the same format as for a project that does not exist.”

parts.statement: All four no-role responses in PRM-A3's scenarios match nonexistent-project status, body and non-exempt headers, with matching formats for the two exempt headers, after the prescribed read of Q.
The same response equivalence holds outside those scenarios, including for existing projects with no comments.

obligations.statement: Each action attempted by a caller with no role leaves the project unchanged.

parts.statement: All four no-role requests in PRM-A3's scenarios preserve the owner's view of the seeded project's title, body, comments and revision list byte-for-byte.
No-role requests preserve the project outside those scenarios, including when it initially has no comments.

rejected.objection: The criteria allow authorization to depend on whether the project has comments.
rejected.reason: PRM-A1 sends each caller's actions to a freshly seeded P, which holds a title, a body, two comments and a revision list. The objection's scenario is another input: the same request on a project with no comments, whose specified outcome under D1 and D2 is the same, the viewer's edit refused with HTTP 403. The criteria fix the cases the check runs, and the standard does not demand a check of every such variant.
